title: Happy-path integration tests don't exercise CRC verification path
description:
In integration.rs, three_parts_in_order calls encode_and_assemble() which does set_expected_crc32(whole_crc), but the whole_crc is computed by crc32fast::hash (self-referential). The test validates that finish() succeeds and returns the expected bytes, but the CRC comparison in finish() is always crc32fast::hash(buffer) == crc32fast::hash(original) — which is trivially true.

A proper happy-path CRC test needs a hardcoded CRC from an independent source (e.g. Python binascii.crc32). For example:
  bytes(range(90)) → Python: binascii.crc32(bytes(range(90))) & 0xFFFFFFFF = 0x4E495A52
  This value should be hardcoded and used as the expected CRC rather than computed by crc32fast.
